Theorem
[local uniqueness of geodesics]

Source: petersen:page-0189 ↗ def:pet-ch5-geodesic

1. ch5:5.2.2Let $I_1,I_2$ be intervals with $t_0\in I_1\cap I_2$. If $c_1:I_1\to U$ and $c_2:I_2\to U$ are geodesics in a chart $U\subset M$ with $c_1(t_0)=c_2(t_0)$ and $\dot c_1(t_0)=\dot c_2(t_0)$, then $c_1|_{I_1\cap I_2}=c_2|_{I_1\cap I_2}$.
Proof

↗ thm:pet-ch5-local-uniqueness \sketch In coordinates set $z_i=(u_i,\dot u_i)$ with $u_i=\varphi \circ c_i$. Both solve $z'=F(z)$, $F(x,w)=(w,-\Gamma _x(w,w))$, and $F$ is locally Lipschitz. The equality set of $z_1,z_2$ is closed and, by local ODE uniqueness, open in $I_1\cap I_2$. It contains $t_0$, hence equals the whole interval.

□
